def: The GPU price per hour divided by the tokens served per hour, times one million; meaningful only with stated batch, context, precision, latency target and utilisation.
The total number of tokens a system generates per second across all concurrent requests.
The share of time a GPU is doing useful work; idle time is billed but produces no tokens.
The number of floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory; a step is memory-bound when this is below the GPU's FLOPs-to-bandwidth ratio.
Limited by how fast bytes can be read from memory rather than by arithmetic, as in small-batch decoding.
Limited by arithmetic throughput rather than memory bandwidth, as in prefill of long prompts.
The maximum acceptable time between streamed tokens, which caps the batch size a GPU can run.
The share of time a rented GPU must be busy for its cost per token to match a per-token API price.
How much busier the busiest period is than the average, which sets how many GPUs must be provisioned.
